content:
**The honest answer first:** the best DHM supplement for most people is a plain, single-ingredient product that tells you exactly how many milligrams of dihydromyricetin (DHM) you get per serving and doesn't charge a premium for extras you can't evaluate. On that basis, **NusaPure** and **Double Wood** give you the most DHM for the money, **DHM Depot** is the best low-dose budget pick, and **No Days Wasted** is the pick if you want a single "night-out" product that bundles DHM with L-cysteine and a few other ingredients. The bigger point is this: DHM is a promising compound with mostly animal and lab research behind it, and there is no good evidence that any brand prevents hangovers in everyone. Buy on dose and price, not on marketing.

**How we compared them:** for each product we looked at the DHM dose per serving, the listed price, the number of servings, and the **price per 100 mg of DHM**, which is the fairest way to compare a 300 mg capsule with a 1,000 mg one. We also looked at what else is in the formula and whether those extras make sense. Prices change often on Amazon, so treat the figures below as a snapshot and check the current listing before you buy. This page is our editorial ranking and buying guide; for the live, side-by-side comparison table with ratings, see our [DHM supplement reviews](/reviews).

> **This is not medical advice.** DHM is a dietary supplement. Supplements are not reviewed by the FDA for safety or effectiveness before they're sold. **Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking DHM if** you take prescription medicines (especially sedatives, sleep medicines, anti-anxiety drugs, blood thinners, or drugs processed by the liver), you are pregnant or breastfeeding, you have liver or kidney disease, or you're under 21. No supplement makes it safe to drive after drinking or to drink more than you otherwise would.

A few things jump out:

- **The spread is huge.** The cheapest DHM in this list costs about a nickel per 100 mg. The most expensive costs more than a dollar. That's roughly a 20-fold difference for the same main ingredient.
- **Combination formulas cost more per milligram of DHM.** Some of that money goes to the extra ingredients. Whether those extras are worth it is a separate question, covered below.
- **Small packs are the most expensive way to buy.** A 4-serving pack is convenient for a trip or a single event, but you pay heavily for that convenience.

## What Is a DHM Supplement?

DHM stands for **dihydromyricetin**, a flavonoid (a type of plant compound) found in several plants. Commercial DHM is usually extracted from **vine tea** (*Ampelopsis grossedentata*), which is naturally rich in it. It's also associated with the **Japanese raisin tree** (*Hovenia dulcis*), which has a long history in traditional East Asian remedies for drinking. Our guide to the [Japanese raisin tree and DHM](/never-hungover/dhm-japanese-raisin-tree-complete-guide) covers the plant's history in more detail.

A DHM supplement is simply a capsule or tablet that delivers a measured amount of that compound. Most products fall into one of three groups:

1. **Single-ingredient DHM.** Just DHM, usually at 300 mg or 1,000 mg per serving. Examples: NusaPure, DHM Depot, Double Wood.
2. **DHM-led blends.** DHM plus a handful of supporting ingredients, often L-cysteine, milk thistle, prickly pear, B vitamins, or electrolytes. Examples: No Days Wasted, Cheers Restore, Flyby.
3. **Liver-support stacks.** DHM combined with other botanicals aimed at general liver health, such as reishi mushroom or milk thistle. Example: Toniiq Ease.

### A labeling trap to watch for: "Hovenia dulcis extract" is not the same as DHM

Some products list **Hovenia dulcis extract** or "Japanese raisin tree extract" rather than dihydromyricetin itself. That isn't automatically bad, but it isn't the same thing. An extract of the plant contains many compounds, and the label often doesn't say how much of it is actually DHM. If the supplement facts panel doesn't state a DHM amount in milligrams, you have no way to know what dose you're getting. All of the products in our table list DHM directly.

## Does DHM Actually Work? What the Research Supports

Before spending money on any brand, it helps to know what DHM can and can't reasonably be expected to do. The short version: the research is genuinely interesting, but most of it comes from animals and lab work, and human evidence for hangovers specifically is thin.

**The rodent research that started the interest.** A widely cited 2012 study by Jing Liang and colleagues at UCLA, published in the *Journal of Neuroscience*, found that DHM reduced signs of alcohol intoxication and withdrawal in rats. The proposed mechanism involves GABA-A receptors in the brain, the same receptors alcohol acts on. This study is the main reason DHM became a "hangover supplement," but it was done in rats, not people.

**Liver and alcohol metabolism in animals.** Later work, including mouse studies from the same research group after it moved to the University of Southern California, reported that DHM supported the enzymes that break down alcohol and its toxic by-product acetaldehyde, and reduced signs of alcohol-related liver stress. Again, promising, but in animals.

**The best human data is about the liver, not hangovers.** A randomized, placebo-controlled trial published in 2015 in *Pharmacological Research* gave DHM to people with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease for three months and found improvements in some liver and metabolic markers compared with placebo. It's encouraging for liver health, but it didn't test hangovers and didn't involve drinking.

**What's missing.** There are no large, independent human trials showing that DHM reliably reduces hangover symptoms. Many people report feeling better when they take it, and that experience counts for something, but it's hard to separate from other things people do on the same night, like drinking more water or pacing themselves. There's also evidence from animal studies that DHM is poorly absorbed when taken by mouth, which is one reason some brands pair it with other ingredients or use larger doses.

Our full breakdown is in [Does DHM work? An honest science review](/never-hungover/does-dhm-work-honest-science-review-2025), and the human studies are summarized in our [DHM clinical trials guide](/never-hungover/dhm-randomized-controlled-trials). The practical takeaway: **treat DHM as a reasonable thing to try, not a guarantee.** That's another reason to buy on value. If it turns out not to help you, you've lost less money.

## The Best DHM Supplements, Brand by Brand

Here's an honest look at each product, with what it does well and where it falls short. All of these are sold on Amazon. We earn a small commission if you buy through our links, at no extra cost to you, and it doesn't change how we rank them.

### Best overall value: NusaPure DHM 1,000 mg

[NusaPure Dihydromyricetin 1,000 mg](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08B32XBRB?tag=dhmguide-20) is the plainest product here and, on current pricing, the cheapest per milligram by a wide margin. You get 60 servings of 1,000 mg DHM and nothing else.

**Pros**
- Lowest price per 100 mg of DHM in our comparison (about $0.05)
- 60 servings in one bottle, enough for months of occasional use
- Single ingredient, so you know exactly what you're taking

**Cons**
- Fewer customer reviews than the bigger brands
- No supporting ingredients, if you want those
- 1,000 mg per serving is more than some people need; there's no easy way to take a smaller dose

**Best for:** anyone who wants straightforward DHM at the lowest cost. More detail in our [NusaPure DHM review](/never-hungover/nusapure-dhm-review-analysis).

### Best-known budget pick: Double Wood DHM

[Double Wood DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20) is one of the longest-running DHM products on Amazon and has a large base of reviews. It delivers 1,000 mg of DHM per serving at around $0.80 a serving.

**Pros**
- 1,000 mg DHM per serving
- About $0.08 per 100 mg, still very good value
- Large review history, so you're not the first person trying it

**Cons**
- Costs more per milligram than NusaPure
- No extra ingredients beyond DHM and minor minerals
- 30 servings per bottle, half the count of NusaPure

**Best for:** people who want a widely used, simple DHM product. See our [Double Wood DHM review](/never-hungover/double-wood-dhm-review-analysis), or the head-to-head [Double Wood vs NusaPure comparison](/never-hungover/double-wood-vs-nusapure-dhm-comparison-2025).

### Best low-dose option: DHM Depot

[DHM Depot](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0767N448Q?tag=dhmguide-20) sells 300 mg capsules, 50 to a bottle, at about $0.40 each.

**Pros**
- Lowest price per serving in the list
- 300 mg capsules make it easy to adjust your dose up or down
- Single ingredient

**Cons**
- At 300 mg per capsule, you'll take two to three capsules to match the 600 to 1,000 mg range many people use, which narrows the price advantage
- Fewer extras and simpler branding than the premium options

**Best for:** people who prefer flexible, smaller doses, or who want to start low. Our [DHM Depot review](/never-hungover/dhm-depot-review-2025) has more.

### Best all-in-one formula: No Days Wasted DHM Detox

[No Days Wasted DHM Detox](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20) pairs 1,000 mg of DHM with L-cysteine, milk thistle, prickly pear, B vitamins, and electrolytes. It's built as a single product for a night out.

**Pros**
- Full 1,000 mg DHM dose
- Includes L-cysteine, which has a small amount of human research on hangover symptoms
- Convenient if you'd rather not combine separate products

**Cons**
- About $1.93 per serving, roughly four times the cost of plain DHM per milligram
- Only 15 servings per pack
- The extra ingredients are mostly at doses where the evidence is limited

**Best for:** people who want one premium product and are fine paying for convenience. See our [No Days Wasted review](/never-hungover/no-days-wasted-dhm-review-analysis).

### Best liver-support stack: Toniiq Ease

[Toniiq Ease](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07S448GTT?tag=dhmguide-20) combines 300 mg of DHM with red reishi mushroom and milk thistle standardized to silymarin.

**Pros**
- 40 servings at about $0.62 each
- Includes milk thistle, the most-studied liver botanical
- Good choice if your interest is general liver support rather than one big night

**Cons**
- Only 300 mg DHM per serving, lower than many people use around drinking
- Three capsules per serving
- Extra ingredients make it harder to tell what, if anything, is helping

**Best for:** regular, moderate drinkers interested in a broader liver formula. More in our [Toniiq Ease review](/never-hungover/toniiq-ease-dhm-review-analysis).

### Cheers Restore

[Cheers Restore](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B079P7FXTW?tag=dhmguide-20) is one of the best-known brands in this category and has thousands of reviews. It combines DHM with L-cysteine, prickly pear, B vitamins, ginger, and vine tea.

- Blend includes several ingredients commonly used around drinking
- Widely available

**Cons**

- Only 12 servings per pack

**Best for:** people who've tried it and like it, or who value the brand. Our [Cheers Restore review](/never-hungover/cheers-restore-review) goes deeper.

**Cons**

**Pros**

- Broad formula if you want many ingredients in one product

**Cons**
- Most expensive per milligram of DHM by far (about $1.21 per 100 mg)
- Only 300 mg DHM per serving
- 4 servings per pack in the listing we track

**Best for:** a one-off trial or travel, not regular use. See our [Flyby Recovery review](/never-hungover/flyby-recovery-review-2025).

## How to Choose a DHM Supplement: Five Things That Matter

Most "best DHM" lists rank products by star rating. Star ratings mostly measure packaging, shipping, and expectations. Here's what actually separates one DHM supplement from another.

### 1. The DHM dose in milligrams

Look for a clearly stated amount of **dihydromyricetin** on the supplement facts panel. If you only see a "proprietary blend" with a total weight, you don't know how much DHM is inside.

### 2. Price per 100 mg of DHM

This is the single most useful number for comparing brands. To work it out:

1. Divide the bottle price by the number of servings to get the price per serving.
2. Divide that by the DHM dose per serving, then multiply by 100.

For example, a $28.99 bottle with 60 servings of 1,000 mg costs about $0.48 a serving, which works out to roughly $0.05 per 100 mg.

### 3. Whether the extras are worth paying for

Common extras and where they stand:

- **L-cysteine:** an amino acid involved in making glutathione, an antioxidant the liver uses. A small Finnish trial published in 2020 reported fewer hangover symptoms in some participants, but the study was small and not definitive.
- **Milk thistle (silymarin):** the most researched liver herb. Human results are mixed, but it's generally well tolerated. See our [DHM vs milk thistle comparison](/never-hungover/dhm-vs-milk-thistle-which-liver-supplement-more-effective-2025).
- **Prickly pear:** an older small study suggested it may reduce some hangover symptoms. Evidence is limited.
- **B vitamins and electrolytes:** cheap to add and harmless at normal doses, but you can get the same benefit from food and a glass of water or an electrolyte drink.

If you'd like these ingredients, a combination product is convenient. If you only want DHM, a single-ingredient product will save you a lot of money.

### 4. Capsule size and count per serving

Some formulas need three capsules for one serving. That matters if you dislike swallowing pills or want to carry a few in your wallet.

### 5. Manufacturing and testing

Look for products made in facilities that follow current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP). Third-party testing is a plus, though brands vary in how much detail they publish. Because supplements aren't approved by the FDA before sale, choosing an established brand with a clear label is the most practical safeguard you have.

## DHM Supplement Dosage: How Much to Take and When

There's no official recommended dose for DHM, since it's a supplement rather than a drug. Commercial products mostly sit between **300 mg and 1,200 mg per serving**, and many people use somewhere around 600 to 1,000 mg on a night they drink.

Common approaches:

- **Before or during drinking:** some people take a dose with their first drink, based on the idea that DHM works best while alcohol is being processed.
- **Before bed:** others take a dose after their last drink, along with water.
- **Split dose:** some take half before and half after.

There's no strong human evidence favoring one timing over another. Start at the lower end of the range, see how you feel, and follow the label. Our [DHM dosage guide](/never-hungover/dhm-dosage-guide-2025) and [DHM dosage calculator](/dhm-dosage-calculator) walk through this based on body weight and how much you plan to drink.

## DHM Supplement Side Effects and Safety

DHM appears to be well tolerated in the studies done so far, and side effects reported by users are usually mild. That said, long-term human safety data is limited.

Reported or possible side effects include:

- Mild stomach upset or nausea
- Drowsiness, especially combined with alcohol
- Headache (which can be hard to separate from drinking itself)

Be more careful, and check with a doctor or pharmacist first, if you:

- **Take sedatives or sleep medicines.** DHM acts on GABA-A receptors in animal studies. Combining it with benzodiazepines, sleep aids, or other sedatives on top of alcohol could add to drowsiness.
- **Take medicines processed by the liver** or blood thinners. Interaction data for DHM in people is limited.
- **Are pregnant or breastfeeding.** There's no safety data, and alcohol should be avoided anyway.
- **Have liver or kidney disease.**

Our [DHM safety guide](/never-hungover/dhm-safety-complete-guide-2025) and [DHM medication interactions guide](/never-hungover/dhm-medication-interactions-safety-guide-2025) cover this in more depth. If you plan to use it often, read [can you take DHM every day?](/never-hungover/can-you-take-dhm-every-day-long-term-guide-2025).

> **When to skip the supplement and get help.** DHM is meant for social drinkers trying to feel better the next day. It is not a treatment for alcohol poisoning or for withdrawal. Call 911 if someone who has been drinking is confused, can't stay awake, is vomiting while drowsy, has slow or irregular breathing, has a seizure, or has bluish or very pale skin. If you get shaky, sweaty, anxious, or have a racing heart when you stop drinking after several days of heavy use, that can be a sign of withdrawal, and it's worth talking to a doctor rather than treating it with supplements.

## DHM Capsules vs Powders vs Drinks

Most DHM is sold as **capsules or tablets**, which are the easiest to dose accurately and carry. You'll also see **powders** and DHM-containing **drinks or shots**.

- **Capsules and tablets:** the simplest option. Dose is printed on the label; easy to travel with.
- **Powders:** often cheaper per gram, but DHM tastes bitter and it's harder to measure small doses without a scale.
- **Drinks and shots:** convenient at a party, but usually expensive per milligram, and DHM content is not always disclosed.

There's no good evidence that one form is absorbed meaningfully better than another in people. Our [DHM product forms comparison](/never-hungover/dhm-product-forms-absorption-comparison-2025) covers the claims brands make about absorption.

## Where to Buy DHM Supplements

DHM is sold mainly online, through Amazon and brand websites. It's less common in pharmacies and grocery stores in the US, although some larger retailers carry one or two brands. Buying online usually gives you more choice and lower prices.

A few tips:

- **Buy from the brand's official listing.** On Amazon, check that the seller is the brand itself or Amazon, to avoid counterfeit or old stock.
- **Check the expiry date** when the bottle arrives.
- **Compare price per 100 mg,** not price per bottle.

If you're outside the US, availability varies by country. Our [DHM availability worldwide guide](/never-hungover/dhm-availability-worldwide-guide-2025) covers where to find it.

## What a DHM Supplement Won't Do

To keep expectations realistic:

- **It won't sober you up.** There is no good evidence that DHM lowers your blood alcohol concentration in people in a way that matters for safety. Never drive after drinking, whatever you've taken.
- **It won't undo heavy drinking.** The amount you drink is still the biggest factor in how you feel the next day and in long-term liver health.
- **It won't replace the basics.** Eating before you drink, alternating with water, and stopping earlier all have better support than any supplement. Our guide on [how to prevent a hangover](/never-hungover/how-to-prevent-a-hangover) covers the habits with the best evidence.

## Our Bottom Line

If you want to try DHM, start with a simple, single-ingredient product and judge it on price per 100 mg of DHM. [NusaPure](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08B32XBRB?tag=dhmguide-20) and [Double Wood](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20) give you full 1,000 mg doses for well under a dollar a serving, and [DHM Depot](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0767N448Q?tag=dhmguide-20) is a good pick if you'd rather start low. If you prefer one product with added L-cysteine and electrolytes and don't mind paying more, [No Days Wasted](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20) is the most complete of the combination formulas.

Whichever you choose, keep your expectations grounded. DHM has interesting research behind it and many people find it helpful, but the drinking itself is still what matters most. Pace yourself, drink water, eat, and check with a pharmacist if you take other medicines.
